title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-03

ai_review.summary: Crisp early‑1966 soundboard recording that captures a high‑energy show, with a smoking Viola Lee Blues and a peppy He Was A Friend Of Mine as highlights.
ai_review.review: The SBD source delivers surprisingly clear audio for a July 3 1966 tape, despite a few occasional cut‑offs and missing tracks. Musically the band is in top form – Jerry’s trippy vocal introductions, tight harmonies on “Dancin’ In The Streets,” and an especially energetic Viola Lee Blues make this a must‑listen early Dead performance.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 4–5 stars, praising both the sound quality and the energetic playing; only a few note minor flaws, yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear for a 1966 SBD; reviewers note occasional cut‑offs and missing songs but overall sound is excellent for the era.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, fast‑moving set typical of mid‑summer ’66 – tight vocal harmonies, upbeat blues numbers and a lively mix that keeps the momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note his trippy, fluttering early vocals and enthusiastic spoken intros (e.g., Viola Lee Blues).
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is described as squealing and driving the blues numbers; no specific comment on Keith or later keyboardists.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming gets special praise on Viola Lee Blues, noted for its propulsive feel.
